name: Ferdinand von Hagen
profile: Listed by Hurun as a GoStudent founder, but public sources name Felix Ohswald and Gregor Müller as GoStudent's founders (Vienna, 2016). A CB Insights entry lists a Ferdinand von Hagen as former CTO of Studienkreis (a German tutoring firm acquired by GoStudent), with GoStudent, Deloitte, ETH Zurich and Airbus in his work history.
notes: Founder attribution looks wrong: he appears to be a tech executive (ex-CTO at Studienkreis, a GoStudent group company), not a co-founder. His current role isn't confirmed. Source: https://www.cbinsights.com/company/studienkreis/people. For GoStudent, the founders are Felix Ohswald (CEO) and Gregor Müller.

name: Chen Yuqi
profile: Chen Yuqi (Richie Chen) co-founded Hai Robotics in Shenzhen in 2016. The company makes autonomous case-handling robots (ACRs) for warehouse automation and was later valued at about $2B. He still runs it as CEO. Its HAIPICK and HaiClimber systems are deployed worldwide for customers such as DHL and Philips.
interesting_fact: Hai Robotics launched HAIPICK, billed as the world's first autonomous case-handling robot. The company says it raises warehouse storage density by 80-130%. Chen was named to Fortune China's 40 Under 40 in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Chen earned a BEng in Electronic and Information Engineering from Hong Kong PolyU in 2012. PolyU calls Hai Robotics the first unicorn nurtured under its entrepreneurship ecosystem.
notes: Known in English as Richie Chen. The company PR inbox is the best route.

name: Tomer Tagrin
profile: Israeli entrepreneur Tomer Tagrin co-founded Yotpo with Omri Cohen in 2011. Yotpo is an e-commerce retention marketing platform for reviews, loyalty and, formerly, SMS/email, and reached a $1.4B valuation in 2021. He still runs it as CEO. In 2025 he refocused the company on Reviews, Loyalty and AI and bought CDP startup Coho AI.
interesting_fact: EY named Tagrin Entrepreneur of the Year 2021 for the New York region. He also writes CommerceGPT, a newsletter on how AI is changing shopping.
deep_cut_fact: Tagrin and Cohen met at Tel Aviv University while finishing a combined electrical engineering and computer science degree. Yotpo's own founding story says Tagrin was burned by fake reviews when buying a camera online.
notes: Active conference speaker (Shoptalk, eTail). Yotpo laid off ~200 staff in Aug 2025 and shut its email/SMS products, so avoid that topic. Best routes: LinkedIn or pr@yotpo.com.

name: Olivier Scialom
profile: French entrepreneur Olivier Scialom co-founded Merama in December 2020 with Sujay Tyle, Felipe Delgado, Renato Andrade and Guilherme Nosralla. Merama is a Latin American e-commerce roll-up that buys majority stakes in leading online brands while their founders keep running them. It raised a $60M Series A and a $225M Series B in 2021 and became a unicorn.
interesting_fact: Merama raised its $225M Series B only about five months after its first round, becoming one of Latin America's fastest e-commerce unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: Before Merama, Scialom co-founded Petsy, a Mexican pet-focused e-commerce site that was sold to Maskota.
notes: Very low public profile and his current role isn't confirmed. Sujay Tyle is the company's public face. No published contact was found. Merama's website (merama.io) returned almost no content.

name: David Cummings
current_role: Founder, Atlanta Tech Village; founder/CEO, Atlanta Ventures
profile: Atlanta serial entrepreneur David Cummings co-founded marketing-automation firm Pardot, which was sold to ExactTarget (later Salesforce) for $95M in 2012. He then co-founded SalesLoft with Kyle Porter. Salesloft reached a $1B+ valuation before Vista Equity bought it. He now runs the Atlanta Tech Village startup hub and the Atlanta Ventures fund.
interesting_fact: Atlanta Tech Village, which he founded, is billed as the Southeast's largest tech entrepreneur center. Its alumni include SalesLoft, Calendly and Terminus. He was an early investor in Calendly.
deep_cut_fact: A Tallahassee, Florida native with an economics degree from Duke, he has founded 10+ companies. Besides software, they include Intown Golf Club, an Atlanta indoor golf venture.
notes: Very accessible. He has blogged on davidcummings.org for years and is active on X. Atlanta Tech Village and Atlanta Ventures are natural routes in.

name: Yanek Korff
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Expel (some Expel pages list him as Chief of Staff)
profile: Security veteran Yanek Korff co-founded Expel, a managed detection and response firm in Herndon, Virginia, with fellow Mandiant alumni Dave Merkel and Justin Bajko around 2016. Expel became a $1B+ unicorn in 2021. Before that, Korff ran Mandiant's managed services business, was CTO of FireEye as a Service, and was responsible for most of AOL's security infrastructure.
interesting_fact: He co-authored the O'Reilly book 'Mastering FreeBSD and OpenBSD Security'.
deep_cut_fact: His IT career began as a student help-desk technician in a 'musty basement' at the College of William and Mary. Expel's bio also says that whenever anything looks about to catch fire, he walks towards it.
notes: He writes on Expel's blog and speaks at SecureWorld events. Sources disagree on his title (COO vs Chief of Staff).

name: Xuyang Ren
current_role: Co-founder, NewsBreak (Particle Media) and Yidian Zixun; angel investor (founded Tianshan Capital in 2015)
profile: Ren Xuyang (任旭阳) was an early Baidu executive and its VP of marketing and business development. He co-founded Chinese news aggregator Yidian Zixun and, with Jeff Zheng, the US local-news app NewsBreak (Particle Media), which reached a $1B+ valuation. Zheng runs NewsBreak as CEO, while Ren is mainly a serial founder and angel investor.
interesting_fact: NewsBreak became one of the most-downloaded news apps in the US. It started out applying the 'interest engine' recommendation approach behind Yidian Zixun's success in China to the American market.
deep_cut_fact: Ren was part of Baidu's early founding-era team. Chinese media also credit him with leading the creation of iQiyi, now one of China's biggest video-streaming platforms, as well as Yidian Zixun.
notes: China-based and low profile in English-language media. Jeff Zheng is NewsBreak's public face. Ren briefly served as Yidian Zixun CEO in early 2019. No personal contact was found.

name: Luca Martinetti
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, TrueLayer (still described as CTO in Oct 2025; stepped down as a UK company director in Jan 2025)
profile: Italian engineer Luca Martinetti co-founded London open-banking payments company TrueLayer in 2016 with Francesco Simoneschi. TrueLayer raised $130M at a $1B+ valuation in 2021. Before that he was a lead data engineer at Plaid. He leads TrueLayer's technology, which is built heavily on Rust, and is also an angel investor.
interesting_fact: TrueLayer was an early adopter of the Rust programming language. Martinetti says modern systems languages like Rust 'will change the way services and applications are built'.
deep_cut_fact: He met co-founder Francesco Simoneschi at school in Rome. He built his own drones before high-spec ones were widely available, joking that his 'engineering skills were maybe not matched to my piloting skills'.
notes: He resigned as a director of TrueLayer Limited on 20 Jan 2025 (https://open.endole.co.uk/insight/company/10278251-truelayer-limited), but FF News still quoted him as CTO in Oct 2025. Check his current title before reaching out. No published press email was found.

name: Gerbert Kaandorp
current_role: Co-founder and Chief R&D, BrainCreators (per Crunchbase; not independently confirmed)
profile: Dutch technologist Gerbert Kaandorp co-founded Amsterdam fintech Backbase with Jouk Pleiter in 2003 and was its CTO for about a decade. Backbase now sells a banking engagement platform to banks worldwide and was valued at about $3B. He has since left Backbase. Crunchbase lists him as co-founder of AI company BrainCreators.
interesting_fact: Backbase, now a 2,500+ person banking-software company, began in 2003 as one of the early Ajax (JavaScript/HTML) web-application frameworks.
deep_cut_fact: Backbase was founded in 2003 by Kaandorp and Jouk Pleiter. It originally made an Ajax framework (based on HTML and JavaScript), years before it moved into digital-banking software.
notes: Low public profile and no longer at Backbase. His current role comes from Crunchbase only (https://crunchbase.com/person/gerbert-kaandorp). No published contact was found. The web search budget ran out during this person, so the profile is thinner.

name: Yang Changle
current_role: Co-founder, Tujia (current executive role not confirmed)
profile: Yang Changle, known in English as Melissa Yang, co-founded Beijing vacation-rental platform Tujia with Justin Luo in December 2011. Tujia raised money from HomeAway, Ctrip, Tencent and others and was valued at $1.5B+ in 2017. It bought rivals Mayi.com and Fishtrip and became China's leading home-sharing platform.
interesting_fact: In 2020 KrASIA reported that Tujia led China's home-sharing market with about 60% share, ahead of Airbnb, Meituan Minsu and Xiaozhu. When Airbnb left mainland China in 2022, Tujia took over some of its hosts.
deep_cut_fact: When she co-founded Tujia (途家, meaning 'home on the way'), she was director of deployment for Microsoft's Bing search engine in Asian markets.
notes: English Wikipedia names the founders as Justin Luo and Melissa Yang. The match to 'Yang Changle' rests on the shared surname and the two-founder team; Chinese sources weren't reachable. Her current role at Tujia (now Trip.com-backed) isn't verified. No published personal contact.

name: Lior Shiff
profile: Lior Shiff co-founded and runs Tripledot Studios, a London mobile-games maker known for casual hits such as Solitaire and Woodoku. In May 2025 Tripledot bought AppLovin's games portfolio for $800M, which it said made it a new multi-billion-dollar global games powerhouse.
interesting_fact: Tripledot took the top spot in the Financial Times' FT1000 ranking of Europe's fastest-growing companies on the back of its 'Solitaire' game. It was also named Best Developer at the Pocket Gamer Mobile Games Awards 2023.
notes: Nasdaq has interviewed him ('The Business of Games: Tripledot Studios', https://www.nasdaq.com/videos/the-business-of-games%3A-tripledot-studios). No press email is published on the company sites. The web search budget was exhausted, so no deep-cut fact was found.

name: Lyu Shiwen
current_role: CEO & CTO, Jenscare Scientific (健世科技, HKEX: 9877)
profile: Lyu Shiwen (吕世文) founded Ningbo-based Jenscare Scientific in 2011 and runs it as CEO and CTO. The company develops minimally invasive transcatheter devices for structural heart disease, including the LuX-Valve tricuspid replacement system and the Ken-Valve aortic valve. Jenscare raised a US$164M Series C and later listed in Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Jenscare's LuX-Valve was the first Chinese product to reach the finals of the TCT Shark Tank innovation competition. It later received US FDA Breakthrough Device designation.
deep_cut_fact: Jenscare's technology for removing immunogenicity from, and preventing calcification of, animal-derived tissue was added to China's Ministry of Science and Technology National Key R&D Program in 2016. The company also won the ISMICS Subramanian Innovation Award.
notes: Low English-language profile. Jenscare is HK-listed, so its IR channels (HKEX filings) are another route. The company's published email uses the domain 'dencare.com', which may be a typo on the site, so verify before using.

name: Luciano Freitas
profile: Luciano Freitas co-founded Facily, a São Paulo social-commerce (group-buying) app, in April 2018 with Diego Dzodan, a former Facebook Latin America VP, and Vitor Zaninotto. In December 2021 Facily became Latin America's first social-commerce unicorn, valued above $1B about three years after launch. Dzodan is the company's CEO and public face.
interesting_fact: Facily grew from 100,000 to 7 million orders a month between December 2020 and December 2021. Its model was inspired by Chinese collaborative-commerce apps such as WeChat and Pinduoduo-style group buying.
notes: Very low public profile and little personal information is available. The web search budget was exhausted, so his background and current role weren't researched further. A route via Facily or CEO Diego Dzodan is likely the best option.

name: Debasish Chakraborty
profile: Debasish Chakraborty co-founded Perfios in 2008 with V.R. Govindarajan. Perfios is a Bengaluru B2B fintech whose bank-statement analysis, KYC and credit-decisioning software is used by Indian and international lenders. It became a unicorn in 2024 and operates across South and Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa. He sits on its board, and Nitin Chugh is group CEO.
interesting_fact: Perfios says it started in 2008 to 'transform the financial landscape of the nation'. Its tools now underpin digital lending decisions for many Indian banks and NBFCs, with operations across 15+ countries.
notes: Low public profile, and the company sometimes spells his name 'Debashish'. Co-founder V.R. Govindarajan is the more public face. The web search budget was exhausted, so no deep-cut fact was found.

name: Hany Rashwan
current_role: Co-founder, 21.co / 21shares (acquired by FalconX, Nov 2025); current title not confirmed
profile: Hany Rashwan co-founded 21shares with Ophelia Snyder in July 2018. The company is a Zurich crypto ETP issuer that launched HODL, the world's first crypto ETP, on SIX Swiss Exchange. Its parent 21.co raised money at up to a $2B valuation in 2022, making it Switzerland's largest crypto unicorn. FalconX acquired 21shares in November 2025, and it now manages $5B+ across 50+ ETPs.
interesting_fact: 21shares launched HODL, the world's first crypto ETP, on SIX Swiss Exchange in November 2018, only four months after the company was founded. It also launched the first staking ETP.
deep_cut_fact: 21shares and CoinGecko jointly created the Global Crypto Classification Standard (GCCS) in 2023, a taxonomy for categorising crypto assets.
notes: His role after the FalconX acquisition isn't verified (the web search budget was exhausted). Co-founder Ophelia Snyder is also a frequent public face.

name: Bobby Balachandran
profile: Bobby Balachandran founded Exterro, a Portland, Oregon legal-GRC software company, and runs it as CEO. Exterro sells eDiscovery, privacy and data governance, digital forensics (it bought AccessData, maker of FTK) and cybersecurity-compliance software. It has about 820 employees in 11 countries and says half the Fortune 100 use it.
interesting_fact: Exterro says half of the Fortune 100 use its software and that it has managed about 800,000 legal holds.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership, Exterro double-matches employee donations to causes such as World Central Kitchen, Black Girls Code and the Ukrainian Red Cross. Employees also volunteer with the Oregon Food Bank and Habitat for Humanity.
notes: Exterro is private and PE-backed (Leeds Equity). No press email is published; the newsroom is at https://www.exterro.com/news-press. The web search budget was exhausted, so his personal background wasn't researched.
